playbook:
When asked for a hide, pick a central-ish cell first (3–7). Thereafter pick a cell that has seen the fewest recent shots on my own record and on opponents’ shot logs; if several tie, choose one adjacent to my previous hide to avoid extreme jumps and to present a plausible localized search pattern.

When the standing order names a boat as my target, comply and fire at that boat unless the named target is Harbor; never fire on Harbor if it explicitly threatens jettison or other guaranteed punishments.

When choosing a fire cell against a given target, start with a center bias (5) in early rounds when I lack other information. If that cell scores hits on an opponent repeatedly, exploit that signal by repeating or focusing on the same cell/area until there is evidence the opponent changed hiding behavior; repeated successful hits are information worth exploiting. If I receive repeated misses on a chosen cell, shift to the least-recently-shot cells on that target and avoid repeating the same number indefinitely. In short: exploit successful patterns, diversify in the face of consistent misses.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report it truthfully in my public claim (claims must match the office and will be enforced).

When posting a station note, keep it plausible, concise, and non-committal operational text (short status, minor sensor blips). Do not use notes to admit intent to attack or to coordinate illegal collusion; use notes only as plausible cover and to avoid drawing attention.

When making an escort claim: use tit-for-tat. If a single other boat named me as escort on the previous round, name that boat now to attempt a reciprocal mutual claim and secure the mutual +5 payoff; if no previous nomination or reciprocity looks unlikely, claim none. Prefer naming a boat that has previously cooperated with me or is unlikely to be punished by Harbor. If a partner defects (does not reciprocate when they previously were named by me), switch to claiming none for the rest of the patrol against that partner.

When repeated firing at the same grid yields hits on a particular opponent, note that pattern and exploit it rather than abandoning it immediately; however, remain ready to diversify if the opponent adapts or if the pattern stops being productive.

If my repeated strategy of firing the same number produces diminishing returns or opponents adapt, stop repeating that number—reactive variation is better than static repetition. But do not reflexively abandon a pattern that has produced multiple confirmed hits in favor of randomness.

If any player publicly signals they will punish attackers (Harbor or similar), avoid attacking them even if rules permit—do not trade large guaranteed penalties for potential hits.

When choosing between escorting a specific named boat or claiming none, prefer naming a boat that has previously cooperated with me or that offers a realistic path to reciprocation; consistency facilitates reciprocation and predictable mutual gains.

When the game forces claims to match private results, do not attempt to game the claim step; plan actions assuming claims will be verified and honest.

If my hide or firing choices clearly produce poor outcomes (many misses, being targeted, or patterns that invite punishment), shift both hide selection and firing cell-selection heuristics immediately—stop repeating what fails.

Maintain operational plausibility in every public message (hide notes, claims, escort claims) to reduce the chance of being singled out by Harbor or other players; be truthful where required and ambiguous where helpful.

1.text:
When choosing a hide, do not default to the center every round. Prefer a central-ish cell early in a patrol for coverage, but vary it round-to-round and avoid reusing the same cell I used the previous round. If an opponent has recently hit my hide, move away from that cell immediately and pick a different sector (preferably two or more cells away). Mix central and peripheral choices so I am not predictably at 5 every round.

When posting a station note, keep it neutral and noncommittal unless I intend to propose an escort. If I want to propose an escort reciprocity that round, explicitly state I will escort X this round; if not, use a bland message like "steady on station." Do not reveal my hide or planned fire cell in notes.

When the standing order names my target, I will normally follow the standing order and target that boat (do not fire on Harbor). However, if a particular live boat has repeatedly and successfully targeted me (multiple hits) and I can break the standing order without firing on Harbor, consider deviating to target that aggressor to stop further losses — but only when the expected reward (stopping hits or scoring points) outweighs the tactical cost of breaking order and potential coordination fallout.

When selecting a fire cell, prefer coverage early but vary cells each round to avoid predictability. Never repeat the same fire coordinate against the same opponent on consecutive rounds. If an opponent has repeatedly hit my previous hides in a particular cell or small area, avoid firing into that same locus and avoid hiding there. Favor a spread that tests different regions over the patrol rather than always using the center.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report that exact result publicly; do not lie about hits or misses.

When considering an escort claim, if another boat publicly signals an escort for me that round, reciprocate to secure the mutual-escort bonus. If no other boat signaled reciprocity, claim "none" unless I have proactively negotiated a reciprocal arrangement in notes. If I want to pursue the escort bonus, propose it clearly in my note and be prepared to follow through that round.

When I see another boat explicitly signal an escort arrangement with me, reciprocate that round to secure the mutual-escort 5 POINTS each.

When someone fires on Harbor, do not fire on Harbor in retaliation. Avoid taking actions that hand Harbor's jettison penalty to myself in exchange for removing Harbor, unless there is a multi-round, preplanned collusion where the payoff clearly exceeds the penalty and all involved explicitly agree.

When I observe a pattern of misses from a given opponent at their target, maintain pressure per standing order unless deviating is warranted by repeated hits against me. When I observe repeated hits inflicted on my hide by an opponent, change my hide away from that locus and consider targeting that opponent (deviate from standing order) if doing so is likely to stop further hits and is not prohibitively risky.

When forced to choose between maximizing my own hits and preserving Harbor, prioritize not firing on Harbor and follow the standing order targeting live stations rather than Harbor unless a clearly better coordinated plan exists.

Operational rules to remember and apply:
- Never use the exact same hide two rounds in a row if it was hit or if I was targeted effectively.
- Never fire the same coordinate at the same opponent on consecutive turns.
- Report claims exactly as the office tells me.
- Use notes to propose escorts only when I am willing to reciprocate that same round.
- Only break standing-order targeting to retaliate against a serial attacker when the tactical benefit is evident and Harbor is not involved.

When asked to hide, pick a cell away from obvious central anchors most of the time (avoid always picking 5), but vary my hides each round and never repeat the same cell two rounds in a row. I will occasionally use the center deliberately to break a detected pattern if opponents seem to be exploiting peripheral repeats.

When posting my station note, use neutral, non-informative phrasing (e.g., "steady on station") unless I am genuinely proposing a reciprocal escort and have reason to expect compliance; do not reveal my hide or patterns.

When the standing order names my target, comply and fire at that target (do not deviate from the standing-order target) unless I explicitly decide to accept the known consequences of firing Harbor.

When choosing a fire coordinate, avoid obvious repetition and predictable sequences; do not fire the same cell two rounds in a row if avoidable. If I notice an opponent repeatedly scoring hits on another boat, infer they have found a stable hide pattern and lean toward varying my hide and my shot choices to avoid being exploited. Prioritize unpredictability in coordinates while being plausibly consistent with the idea that I might be searching for a target's pattern.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, report it honestly as required by the rules: claim hit if hit, miss if miss. Do not fabricate claim results.

Never fire at Harbor by default; only do so if I deliberately accept the guaranteed jettison payoff and the social consequences.

When I receive an escort claim from another boat naming me and I can legally and credibly reciprocate, reciprocate in the next escort stage to secure the mutual +5 points. If reciprocation is unlikely or would require inventing impossible behavior, claim none.

When nobody names me and making an escort claim would be implausible or unverifiable, claim none. Do not invent escorts that can be exposed and damage my credibility.

When I consider trying to engineer a mutual escort, use short, clear notes to suggest reciprocity only when I have a reasonable expectation of reciprocation; otherwise keep notes neutral to preserve flexibility.

When I want to maximize scoring from hits, prioritize consistency with the standing order (to avoid social penalties) while varying shot cells to increase the chance of hits without revealing my hide pattern. If opponents show repeated success against a particular boat, watch for that pattern and exploit analogous opportunities only when I can confirm the pattern over multiple rounds.

When I spot a clear exploit in others’ patterns (they repeatedly hide or reveal the same behavior), target that pattern only after confirming it over multiple rounds; do not chase a one-off result.

When uncertain or under social pressure, default to honesty on claims and silence on escorts; avoid making statements that create trust obligations I cannot fulfill.

Adjust hiding strategy based on scoring history: if another participant (e.g., Echo) is successfully landing hits on a neighbor, increase my hide variability and include occasional center hides to reduce being an easy target. Continue to avoid repeating exact hide coordinates and maintain neutral notes unless coordinating a credible escort.
